contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #007: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture.
Coefficient-uniform resolution of q:forest-code in the staged September 24, 2026 manuscript; this is one combinatorial dependency, not either main correlation theorem.

definitions.pattern: partition of n ordered positions, represented by a restricted-growth word
definitions.joint_pair: the two vectors e_z and v(i)-v(i_prime) for two lit occurrences; all vectors of selected pairs must be jointly independent
definitions.admissible_geometry: at most B disjoint lit blocks covering all but I positions, interval-shaped label occurrences, and nonzero coefficient sum in every constant run

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 007 (Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture.; papers: Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/007.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Over any field, an inclusion-maximal jointly independent collection of m lit-occurrence pairs has a 2m-dimensional span. A coordinate-image basis of its quotient omits 2m labels, and every regular label has all lit starts on one affine line in its nonzero independent quotient direction.
The incidence graph of the regular lines and distinct transition points is a forest. Every regular segment with nonzero run increments is the unique simple path between its endpoint line vertices.

Four position masks, a typed ordered forest, endpoint pairs, omitted representatives and imperfect-position representatives determine the whole equality pattern, including labels appearing only at imperfect positions, independently of every numerical coefficient.

For n>=1,r>=1, a single coefficient-free code space has size at most 2^(10n+3)(2n)^((6r-4)B+I). Its decoder yields an injection of the union over all admissible coefficient witnesses by choosing the first code decoding to each pattern.

For n>=1,r>=1,B>=0,I>=0, the union over all fields, coefficients, lit sets and block choices with the stated admissible geometry and no r jointly independent lit-occurrence pairs has at most 2^(10n+3)(2n)^((6r-4)B+I) equality patterns, with one coefficient-free injective encoding and explicit decoder.

Every literal lit-consistent nonzero-integrand term in q:forest-code supplies blocks satisfying the structural theorem: all block positions are lit, label occurrences are intervals, run sums are nonzero, I<=S_1+U and B<=2k/s+I+2. No translated-residue independence is assumed.

For every admissible numerical coefficient and padding choice in the literal q:forest-code hypotheses and L>=1024, one universal set contains all column patterns and has size at most exp(2048k); the combined column patterns number at most exp(2048Jk). This does not independently establish a main correlation theorem.

The directly checked literature comparator counts t-predictable words with bounded multiplicities and variable-neighbour complexity; it is not the arbitrary-coefficient low-joint-pair-rank theorem. No global novelty conclusion follows from this bounded comparison.

claims.natural_statement: The arbitrary-field maximal-pair quotient saturation, nonzero regular increment and independent-polygon exclusion, all-length nonbacktracking forest endpoint decoder, record-slot bound, exact finite code cardinality, and existential coefficient-witness union injection/cardinality under one shared decode law are formalized by the declarations in research/forest_coding/statement_fidelity.md. This claim does not assert a fully formalized implementation of the witness encoder or either correlation theorem.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open Function

namespace ForestCoding

section Linear

variable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]

theorem dependent_pair_saturates (e w : V) (he : e ≠ 0)
    (hmax : ¬ LinearIndependent K ![e, w]) :
    ∃ c : K, w = c • e := by
  by_contra h
  apply hmax
  apply (LinearIndependent.pair_iff' he).2
  intro c hc
  exact h ⟨c, hc.symm⟩

theorem maximal_pair_saturates {ι : Type*} (old : ι → V)
    (hold : LinearIndependent K old) (e w : V)
    (he : (Submodule.span K (Set.range old)).mkQ e ≠ 0)
    (hmax : ¬ LinearIndependent K (Sum.elim old ![e, w])) :
    ∃ c : K, (Submodule.span K (Set.range old)).mkQ w =
      c • (Submodule.span K (Set.range old)).mkQ e := by
  let D := Submodule.span K (Set.range old)
  apply dependent_pair_saturates (D.mkQ e) (D.mkQ w) he
  intro hpair
  apply hmax
  apply (linearIndependent_span hold).sumElim_of_quotient ![e, w]
  have hfun : (D.mkQ ∘ ![e, w]) = ![D.mkQ e, D.mkQ w] := by
    funext i
    fin_cases i <;> rfl
  change LinearIndependent K (D.mkQ ∘ ![e, w])
  rw [hfun]
  exact hpair

theorem regular_run_nonzero {ι : Type*} (u : ι → V)
    (hu : LinearIndependent K u) (z : ι) (c : K) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    c • u z ≠ 0 := by
  exact smul_ne_zero hc (hu.ne_zero z)

theorem independent_balance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (u : ι → V) (hu : LinearIndependent K u) (c : ι → K)
    (hbalance : ∑ i, c i • u i = 0) :
    ∀ i, c i = 0 := by
  exact Fintype.linearIndependent_iff.mp hu c hbalance

theorem independent_polygon_impossible {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (u : ι → V) (hu : LinearIndependent K u)
    (start finish : ι → V) (c : ι → K)
    (hstep : ∀ i, finish i - start i = c i • u i)
    (hclosed : ∑ i, (finish i - start i) = 0)
    (hnonzero : ∀ i, c i ≠ 0) : False := by
  have hbalance : ∑ i, c i • u i = 0 := by
    simpa only [hstep] using hclosed
  obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty ι›
  exact hnonzero i (independent_balance u hu c hbalance i)

end Linear

section Paths

variable {Vertex : Type*}

noncomputable def endpointDecoder (G : SimpleGraph Vertex) (a b : Vertex) :
    Option (List Vertex) := by
  classical
  exact if h : G.Reachable a b then some h.some.toPath.val.support else none

theorem endpointDecoder_correct (G : SimpleGraph Vertex) (hG : G.IsAcyclic)
    {a b : Vertex} (p : G.Walk a b)
    (hp : List.IsChain (· ≠ ·) p.edges) :
    endpointDecoder G a b = some p.support := by
  classical
  have hpath : p.IsPath := (hG.isPath_iff_isChain p).2 hp
  have heq := hG.path_unique p.reachable.some.toPath ⟨p, hpath⟩
  simp only [endpointDecoder, dif_pos p.reachable]
  exact congrArg (fun q : G.Path a b => some q.val.support) heq

theorem nonbacktracking_walk_unique (G : SimpleGraph Vertex) (hG : G.IsAcyclic)
    {a b : Vertex} (p q : G.Walk a b)
    (hp : List.IsChain (· ≠ ·) p.edges)
    (hq : List.IsChain (· ≠ ·) q.edges) : p = q := by
  exact congrArg Subtype.val
    (hG.path_unique ⟨p, (hG.isPath_iff_isChain p).2 hp⟩
      ⟨q, (hG.isPath_iff_isChain q).2 hq⟩)

theorem endpointDecoder_labels (G : SimpleGraph Vertex) (hG : G.IsAcyclic)
    {a b : Vertex} (p : G.Walk a b)
    (hp : List.IsChain (· ≠ ·) p.edges) (isLine : Vertex → Bool) :
    (endpointDecoder G a b).map (List.filter isLine) =
      some (p.support.filter isLine) := by
  rw [endpointDecoder_correct G hG p hp]
  rfl

end Paths

def recordBudget (r B I : ℕ) := (6 * r - 4) * B + I

def Code (n r B I : ℕ) :=
  (Fin (4 * n) → Bool) × Fin (2 ^ (6 * n + 3)) ×
    (Fin (recordBudget r B I) → Fin (2 * n))

abbrev Pattern (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Fin n

theorem record_budget {r d B I actualI S O : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hd : d ≤ 2 * r - 2) (hS : S ≤ (d + 1) * B)
    (hO : O ≤ d * B) (hI : actualI ≤ I) :
    2 * S + O + actualI ≤ recordBudget r B I := by
  have hcoeff : 3 * d + 2 ≤ 6 * r - 4 := by omega
  calc
    2 * S + O + actualI ≤ (3 * d + 2) * B + I := by nlinarith
    _ ≤ (6 * r - 4) * B + I :=
      Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.mul_le_mul_right B hcoeff) I

theorem code_card (n r B I : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Code n r B I) =
      2 ^ (10 * n + 3) * (2 * n) ^ recordBudget r B I := by
  simp only [Code, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin,
    Fintype.card_bool]
  rw [← mul_assoc, ← pow_add]
  have he : 4 * n + (6 * n + 3) = 10 * n + 3 := by omega
  rw [he]

theorem coefficient_uniform_injection {Witness : Type*}
    (n r B I : ℕ) (valid : Witness → Pattern n → Prop)
    (emit : ∀ w p, valid w p → Code n r B I)
    (decode : Code n r B I → Option (Pattern n))
    (hdecode : ∀ w p h, decode (emit w p h) = some p) :
    ∃ encode : {p : Pattern n // ∃ w, valid w p} → Code n r B I,
      Injective encode := by
  classical
  let encode : {p : Pattern n // ∃ w, valid w p} → Code n r B I :=
    fun p => emit (Classical.choose p.property) p.val (Classical.choose_spec p.property)
  refine ⟨encode, ?_⟩
  intro p q heq
  apply Subtype.ext
  have hp : decode (encode p) = some p.val := hdecode _ _ _
  have hq : decode (encode q) = some q.val := hdecode _ _ _
  exact Option.some.inj (hp.symm.trans ((congrArg decode heq).trans hq))

theorem coefficient_uniform_card {Witness : Type*}
    (n r B I : ℕ) (valid : Witness → Pattern n → Prop)
    (emit : ∀ w p, valid w p → Code n r B I)
    (decode : Code n r B I → Option (Pattern n))
    (hdecode : ∀ w p h, decode (emit w p h) = some p) :
    Nat.card {p : Pattern n // ∃ w, valid w p} ≤
      2 ^ (10 * n + 3) * (2 * n) ^ recordBudget r B I := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨encode, hinj⟩ := coefficient_uniform_injection n r B I valid emit decode hdecode
  calc
    Nat.card {p : Pattern n // ∃ w, valid w p} ≤ Nat.card (Code n r B I) :=
      Nat.card_le_card_of_injective encode hinj
    _ = 2 ^ (10 * n + 3) * (2 * n) ^ recordBudget r B I := by
      rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, code_card]

end ForestCoding

routes.retired_because: Uniformly bounded separate coefficient fibres can have an arbitrarily large union; the route does not establish a common code universe. This is a rejected inference, not a manuscript assertion or a refutation.
